author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Orange Line service between Forest Hills and Back Bay will be suspended for five consecutive days beginning Thursday, September 10, as work continues on the Ruggles Station Improvements Project.

The closure runs through Monday, September 14. Free, accessible shuttle buses will stop between Forest Hills and Back Bay, but riders should expect crowding and longer trips. Boston’s advisory says a Forest Hills rider heading to Downtown Crossing should budget at least 30 extra minutes.

Commuter Rail trips between Forest Hills, Ruggles, Back Bay and South Station will be fare-free during the shutdown. The trip from Forest Hills to Back Bay takes about 10 minutes, although rail schedules may make that alternative more practical for some trips than others.

All replacement buses are accessible, but weekday service may include lift-equipped coach buses; weekend shuttles will use low-floor, ramp-equipped vehicles. Riders should check current MBTA alerts before leaving because the city’s closure calendar covers planned diversions rather than live conditions. Regular Orange Line service north of Back Bay is expected to continue.
dek: Free shuttle buses and fare-free Commuter Rail service will cover the September 10–14 closure for work at Ruggles Station.
headline: Five-day Orange Line shutdown starts Thursday between Forest Hills and Back Bay
